questions.explanation: 15.8% a year is healthy growth: Jio Platforms Limited's customers are buying more each year.

questions.question: Jio Platforms Limited owes 0.21 rupees of loans for every rupee of its owners' money. Which is closest to the truth?

choices.text: Its loans are small to manageable next to what the owners have put in.
Its loans are heavy: lenders have more riding on it than its owners.
Loans never matter for a company that makes a profit.

questions.explanation: At 0.21 rupees of loans per rupee of owners' money, Jio Platforms Limited's owners have more in the business than its lenders.

questions.question: Big institutions asked for 65.4x the shares kept for them. Why do people watch this figure?

choices.text: Professionals who studied the company closely are showing how keen they are.
It guarantees the share price will rise on listing day.
It tells you how many shares you will be given.

questions.explanation: Institutions do the most homework, and they asked for 65.4x their quota of Jio Platforms Limited: strong appetite. Still, no figure guarantees a listing gain.

questions.question: An unofficial grey market premium of ₹248 a share is being quoted. How much should you rely on it?

choices.text: Completely: it tells you the listing price.
A little at most: it is unregulated and easy to push around.
It is set by the stock exchange.

questions.explanation: The grey market premium of ₹248 for Jio Platforms Limited is gossip with a number on it: nobody regulates it, and it often turns out wrong.
